hints: Focus on oxidation numbers, reduction means the oxidation number goes down by gaining electrons.
In reaction 1, work out Cl in $\text{NaClO}$ (+1) and in $\text{NaCl}$ (-1) to see the change.
Check N in $\text{NH}_3$ versus $\text{LiNH}_2$, and ethanol to ethanal, to see if either oxidation number falls or if oxidation happens instead.
walkthrough:
**Recall what reduced means**

Reduction is gain of electrons. That shows up as a decrease in oxidation number.

Rule to use:
$$\text{reduction = oxidation number decreases}$$

**Check reaction 1, Cl in NaClO**

In $\text{NaClO}$, Na is +1 and O is -2, so Cl must be +1 to balance. In $\text{NaCl}$, Cl is -1.

Calculation:
$$+1 \text{ (in NaClO)} \to -1 \text{ (in NaCl)}$$

**Decide reaction 1**

The oxidation number falls from +1 to -1, so Cl gains electrons. This is reduction, so 1 is included.

**Check reaction 2, N in NH3**

In $\text{NH}_3$, H is +1, so N is -3. In $\text{LiNH}_2$, Li is +1 and H is +1, so N is still -3.

Calculation:
$$-3 \text{ (in NH}_3) \to -3 \text{ (in LiNH}_2)$$

**Check reaction 3, ethanol**

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ changes to $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$. This is loss of hydrogen, a classic organic oxidation. The oxidising agent $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ is itself reduced, not the alcohol.

So ethanol is oxidised, not reduced. Only reaction 1 qualifies.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean all three underlined species are reduced. Reaction 2 shows no change in N oxidation number (-3 to -3) and reaction 3 is oxidation of ethanol to ethanal.
options.B: Incorrect. Reaction 1 is correct, but reaction 2 is not. Students sometimes think $\text{NH}_3$ is reduced because $\text{H}_2$ forms, but it is H (+1 to 0) that is reduced, while N stays at -3.
options.C: Incorrect. Neither 2 nor 3 is reduction. Reaction 3 is a well known oxidation with acidified dichromate, orange to green, where ethanol is the reducing agent.
options.D: Correct. Only 1 is reduction. Cl goes from +1 in $\text{NaClO}$ to -1 in $\text{NaCl}$, a decrease in oxidation number. N is unchanged in 2, and ethanol is oxidised in 3.
